html:
A Japanese animated film of 2001 written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki and made by Studio Ghibli. A ten-year-old girl, Chihiro, wanders into a world of spirits, where her parents are turned into pigs; she must work in a bathhouse run by the witch Yubaba to free them.

The film draws on Japanese folklore and on Shinto ideas of spirits living in rivers and places. Its scenes, such as the polluted river spirit and the quiet train across the water, are drawn by hand with great care.

It became the highest-grossing film in Japanese history, a record it held for nineteen years. In 2003 it won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature, the first anime to do so. It helped make Japanese animation a global art form, part of a long line of Japanese images loved abroad that runs back to The Great Wave and the Japonisme craze of the 1800s.
